model_result.answer_summary: Box (a) increases. The rate of CO formation per gram of loaded C3N4 is TOF(omega) x (omega/100) x N_A / M_cat, proportional to omega x TOF. Across the measured points of the Q8-3 diagram the product omega x TOF climbs from 6.2 (% . h^-1) at omega_cat = 0.1% to ~31 at 2.9% and 30.4 at 3.8%, i.e. a net ~4.9-fold increase even though TOF itself falls from 62 to 8 h^-1. The increase is strict through every interior measured step and robust at the endpoints under the half-quantum measurement tolerance; only the final small step (2.9% -> 3.8%) is not sign-determined by the integer displays, which is proven honestly in the Lean file.
assumptions: Rate per gram = TOF x catalyst molecules per gram, from the problem-stated TOF definition on page Q8-2 (number of product molecules per active catalyst molecule per hour) combined with the mass-fraction definition of omega_cat and M_cat = 557.21 g/mol (problem 8.5) and N_A = 6.022e23 mol^-1 (official constants page G1-3).

Data points (omega_cat %, TOF h^-1) = (0.1,62), (0.3,56), (0.6,37), (1,29), (2,15), (2.9,11), (3.8,8) read from the diagram on Q8-3, cross-anchored by the text statement TOF = 8 h^-1 at omega_cat = 3.8% on page Q8-2.

Integer TOF labels are treated as displays with half-quantum tolerance +/-0.5 per the project measurement convention (IChO2026Chem.Reporting); the endpoint conclusion is proven for all toleranced values, while displayed values are used for the interior chain.
Standard Lean logical axioms only (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound); N_A and M_cat are inputs, not axioms.
